sections.html:
Lakeland is the seat of Lanier County, a lake-country place where Banks Lake, Grand Bay Lake and Lake Irma anchor the fishing reputation and Banks Lake National Wildlife Refuge protects more than 4,000 acres of water, marsh and swamp. Moody Air Force Base, the hospital and a large state correctional facility are among the local sources of jobs. Land area is 196.54 square miles, a density of 50.3 residents per square mile.

The county is growing. The mid-2025 estimate of 10,623 residents is 7.6% above the 2020 count of 9,877. A typical owned home is worth $162,300, and 73.2% of homes are lived in by their owners, which leaves a real market for rental houses. With only 39 residential permits in 2025, a seller faces mostly other resale homes. The average household holds 2.82 people and 23.4% of residents are under 18, so family buyers are common.

Monthly owner costs run $1,491 with a mortgage and $443 without, against a $913 median rent. Stability is high: 89.6% of residents stayed in the same house over the prior year.

Lanier's county offices cluster along West Main Street, Lakeland, GA 31635.

  • Tax Commissioner, 56 W Main St, Suite 1, (229) 482-3795: weekdays, 8 until noon and 1 until 5, closed over the lunch hour. Collects property tax and renews tags for the state.
  • Tax Assessor, Suite 2, (229) 482-2090: weekdays 8 to 5, parcel records on qPublic.
  • Board of Commissioners, Suite 9, (229) 482-2088.
  • Probate, (229) 482-3668, and Superior Court, (229) 482-3594.

The county's GovtWindow page takes online payment, and office details are posted at laniercountyboc.com.

sections.h2: Other offices that help a seller
sections.html:
Several more desks matter in a sale. Estates go to Probate at (229) 482-3668, while recorded deeds and liens sit with the clerk at (229) 482-3594. The Magistrate Court number is (229) 482-2207, the Extension Office is at (229) 482-3895 for questions about farm and woodland, and the Sheriff's Office is at (229) 482-3545.

The county's website also has planning and zoning, code enforcement and business license pages, useful if a property needs repairs or has a commercial use. Parcel maps run through qPublic, a free lookup that lets you confirm acreage and the owner of record before quoting a price.

December 20 is the baseline in Georgia. Counties may move it to December 1 or November 15 or divide the bill, so call the Tax Commissioner at (229) 482-3795 for the date on your bill.

Interest is held back for 60 days after the postmark, and penalties can attach to what stays open. A sale in February does not move the burden: whoever held title January 1 owes the year, and Georgia refunds nothing for partial-year ownership. Liens for unpaid county tax are recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court, which is where a title examiner will look.

Mobile homes keep a separate schedule. A location permit is due within 30 days of placement and renews between January 1 and April 1, and the January 1 owner returns the home to the commissioner by April 1.

Lanier County has only the statewide exemptions, with no local add-ons. These are the standard homestead exemption and the disabled veteran exemption, which reaches both city and county tax.

  • Apply at the county tax office once the house is your primary residence.
  • A form that lands after April 1 misses that tax year.
  • Commercial and industrial inventory can be exempt where voters approved a freeport exemption, which the assessors process.

An exemption renews itself only until ownership or residence changes, so a buyer moving in files a fresh application by April 1. As the seller, ask the commissioner whether your exemption was active so the closing figures reflect it.

A real property notice goes out every year, and you have 45 days from its mailing to dispute the fair market value. The first step is a letter to the board of tax assessors. Email counts only if the county has a written policy consenting to electronic service, so mail it unless the assessors confirm otherwise at (229) 482-2090.

The letter must name a route: the county's equalization board, a hearing officer or an arbitrator. A uniform state form exists, and Revenue Department staff cannot overrule the local decision on one parcel.

sections.h2: Selling when back taxes are owed
sections.html:
Request a payoff from the commissioner and ask whether a lien is on file. If the buyer finances, the lender's security instrument is recorded within 90 days, and the state recording tax is $1.50 per $500 (or fraction) of the note.

Heirs should talk to Lanier County Probate about opening the estate before listing. Out-of-town cash buyers can generally accept a payoff deducted at the closing table.

The sequence is short. Get the payoff, check the Clerk for a lien, close, and let the closing attorney pay the commissioner from proceeds. Keep the paid receipt with your closing papers, and tell the assessors about the sale so the next bill reaches the new owner.

sections.h2: Before you list a Lanier County house
sections.html:
A few errands save trouble later. Pull your parcel record on qPublic to confirm acreage and the owner of record, then call the Tax Commissioner for a current payoff and the Tax Assessor to confirm your exemption status. If the house sits on land with a farm or woodland history, the Extension Office can answer questions about how the land has been used.

Tell buyers up front what the yearly tax has been, and keep copies of the last few bills in your listing folder. Lakeland sellers who show a paid-up history and a clear title tend to move faster, because the buyer's lender has less to chase. For a mobile home, confirm the location permit is current and that the January 1 owner has returned it to the commissioner by April 1.

If the buyer is moving in as a primary resident, remind them to file their own homestead application by April 1, since your exemption does not carry over to a new owner. On a lake or refuge property, look at the survey and any easements before you set a price.

faqs.q: Where can I pay property tax in person in Lanier County?
faqs.a: At the Tax Commissioner, 56 W Main St, Suite 1, Lakeland, GA 31635. The phone is (229) 482-3795, and the office is open weekdays 8 to noon and 1 to 5.

faqs.q: What due date does Lanier County use for real estate tax?
faqs.a: Georgia's baseline of December 20 applies unless the county picked December 1, November 15 or installments, so call (229) 482-3795 to confirm. Interest starts 60 days after the postmark.

faqs.q: Does Lanier County add its own homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. State exemptions and the disabled veteran exemption are available if the application arrives by April 1.

faqs.q: How much is a house worth in Lanier County at the median?
faqs.a: $162,300, the 2020-2024 Census median for owner-occupied homes. Rent runs $913 a month at the median, and 73.2% of housing units are owner-occupied.

faqs.q: Is an emailed Lanier County appeal accepted?
faqs.a: Only when the assessors have a written policy allowing electronic service. If not, mail it within 45 days of the notice. The assessor's number is (229) 482-2090.
